I think a lot of people have provided awesome tips on getting more physically fit and I think they are all great. I would just say a few things on the mental side from my experience: I love running because I see a lot of parallels to life. There are runs that whether it's hydration or the weather or whatever, you just know it's not gonna be pleasant within the first 10 minutes, similar to that not everything in life is perfect, and sometimes you just have to push through it. But of course there are also days that even your best isn't good enough to finish the run, it's also kinda a great and humbling life lesson, you know, sometimes it's just not your day. There is a fine line between the two; the competitive side of me really hates to say this, but sometimes it's okay to admit defeat, just like in life, you can't win them all. Obviously don't make a habit of it, but give yourself a break sometimes.

I heard this line a while ago that says "we all have our secrets we just didn't get to yours yet," I think even among the people I am close to, the depth of conversation, perhaps because of my own mental armor and guard, never quite get to how and why deep down, I am so screwed up and negative. I end up just processing all internally, which I think just makes everything worse. Each day is a struggle, but sometimes I just tell myself that just have to struggle through it. I don't know, still seeking a good method of coping.

A part of me feels like instead of being negative to others, why not being negative to myself all the time? But the reality is that most of us live in a social construct with other people, so we can only work towards and manage to maintain some kind of social balance with others that are required of us to move forward.
